You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

What do you mean by “old car makers”? Here are a few common interpretations—tell me which one you want (and any cutoff year), and I’ll tailor the exact query:

1) **Makers with the oldest cars in the dataset** (based on `cars_data.Year`)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year_in_data,
  COUNT(*)      AS cars_count
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC, cars_count DESC;
```

2) **Cars from “old years” and which makers made them** (you choose the cutoff; example: `<= 1975`)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  cd.Year,
  COUNT(*) AS cars_count
FROM cars_data cd
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Model  = cn.Model
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id     = ml.Maker
WHERE cd.Year <= 1975
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName, cd.Year
ORDER BY cd.Year ASC, cars_count DESC;
```

3) **Top N makers with the earliest first appearance** (example: top 10)
```sql
WITH maker_years AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
)
SELECT *
FROM maker_years
ORDER BY first_year ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

Questions to confirm:
- Do you mean **oldest by car year in this dataset**, or **historically old companies** (which this schema may not store)?
- If it’s by car year, what cutoff year (e.g., **<= 1975**) or do you want the **earliest year per maker**?
Focus on makers that produced vehicles a long time ago.

```sql
-- Makers that produced vehicles a long time ago (earliest cars in the dataset)
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS year_span,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicle_records
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
HAVING MIN(cd.Year) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, year_span DESC, vehicle_records DESC;
```

If you want only “long time ago” makers under a specific cutoff (e.g., earliest year <= 1970), tell me the year and I’ll add that filter.
Make sure at least some cars were produced in the year 1970.

```sql
-- Makers that have at least one car in 1970, plus their overall earliest/latest years
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicle_records,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cars_in_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, vehicle_records DESC;
```
make sure to include the name of each matching car maker too

```sql
-- Car makers with at least one car produced in 1970, including maker name
SELECT
  cm.Id AS maker_id,
  cm.Maker AS maker_name,
  cm.FullName AS maker_full_name,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicle_records,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cars_in_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, vehicle_records DESC;
```
